hero.title: POST GRADUATION IN CHEMICAL ENGINEERING IN FRANCE
hero.subtitle: **Studying Postgraduate (PG) Chemical Engineering in France** is a great chance for students who wish to acquire advanced technical knowledge and professional skills in chemical processes, industrial production, process design, materials science, energy systems, and sustainable manufacturing. French universities and engineering schools offer specialized master’s programs combining scientific principles, laboratory work, process modeling, industrial projects and research.

overview: **Studying Postgraduate (PG) Chemical Engineering in France** is a great chance for students who wish to acquire advanced technical knowledge and professional skills in chemical processes, industrial production, process design, materials science, energy systems, and sustainable manufacturing. French universities and engineering schools offer specialized master’s programs combining scientific principles, laboratory work, process modeling, industrial projects and research.

France is an attractive destination for students looking to pursue a ****Master in Chemical Engineering in France****, with openings in the chemicals, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, biotechnology, energy, food processing, and environmental technology sectors. Overseas students can choose to specialize in **chemical process engineering, bioprocessing, green chemistry, industrial safety or process optimisation**, depending on their academic interests and career aspirations.

Students can find ****Chemical Engineering courses in France**** that suit their interests, know about the admission process and get ready for their adventure of studying abroad with the help of ****Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance****.

sections.title: 1. What is the duration of a postgraduate chemical engineering degree in France?

items: In France, a national **Master's degree in Chemical Engineering** is usually a two-year degree (M1 and M2) corresponding to 120 ECTS credits. Engineering diplomas and specialized programs can vary in length and have different entry routes.

sections.title: 2. Is IELTS required for masters in chemical engineering in France?

items: Not all the time. **French master's programs taught in English in France** may require IELTS, TOEFL or another accepted test or approved evidence of prior education in English. French-taught programs may require the student to know French well.

sections.title: 3. What is the cost of PG in Chemical Engineering in France?

items: The benchmark annual fee for a national master’s at eligible public institutions is €255 (€3,950 for non-EU students liable to differentiated fees) for 2026–2027. This is different for engineering schools and other specialized programs .

sections.title: 4.  What jobs can I get after doing a PG in chemical engineering in France?

items: Graduates can be employed in **process engineering, chemical manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, bioprocessing, process safety, environmental technology, energy and research and development**.

sections.title: 5. Which are the universities in France that offer post graduation in Chemical Engineering?

items: Students can explore schools such as **Université de Lorraine – ENSIC, Toulouse INP–ENSIACET, Université Paris-Saclay**. Please check the official websites of the universities for the availability of programs, specializations and admission requirements.

Applicants should contact the institution of their choice to determine the precise qualification it offers before accepting an offer.

The **French national master's degree (diplôme national de master)** is recognized in the French higher education system and in the European higher education area. It usually refers to five years of post-secondary study combined with the prior bachelor’s level study.

An engineering diploma ( *diplôme d'ingénieur* ) is a different type of qualification. Prospective students taking engineering-school programs should make sure that the institution has been authorized and that the **Commission des titres d’ingénieur (CTI) recognition status** is applicable.
**Before you enroll, make sure:**
- The official degree title and awarding institution.
- Level of the program (national master’s degree, engineering diploma or specialization degree).
- Duration of the program and credits.
- The institution’s accreditation or recognition status.
- Acknowledgment of your qualifications for employment or further education in the country you intend to work or study in.

sections.title: 9. Salary and Job Opportunities After Chemical Engineering PG in France**

items: A postgraduate qualification in ****Chemical Engineering in France**** can lead to work in industrial process design, manufacturing, research, energy, biotechnology and environmental technology. It is contingent upon what you specialize in, what practical experience you have, how good your language skills are, where you live and what the employer wants.
Job opportunities for a Chemical Engineering PG in France are:
* Chemical Process Engineer
* Process Design Engineer
* Production Engineer
* Chemical Plant Operations Engineer
* Process Simulation Engineer
* Research and Development Engineer
* Bioprocess Engineer
* Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Engineer
* Quality Assurance or Quality Control Engineer
* Environmental Process Engineer
* Process Safety Engineer
* Energy and Sustainability Engineer
Potential employers are **chemical manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, food processing, biotechnology, energy, materials, water treatment, and engineering consulting.**
**Salary After PG in Chemical Engineering In France**

There is not a single salary for all **** Chemical Engineering graduates in France ****. Compensation varies depending on the role, location, employer, experience, technical specialization and type of contract.
French language skills may be advantageous for roles in plant operations, industrial safety, production coordination, or positions involving local regulations or working with French-speaking teams.

sections.title: 10. Required Documents for Chemical Engineering PG in France**

items: For students applying for ****Chemical Engineering postgraduate in France****, the following documents are usually required:
- Passport valid.
- Bachelor’s degree certificate or provisional degree certificate.
- Transcripts (official)
- CV or résumé.
- Motivation Letter (Statement of Purpose).
- Letters of recommendation, if required.
- English language test results, where applicable.
- Certificate in French, as appropriate.
- Course Syllabus or descriptions available upon request.
- Details of applicable technical projects and internships.
- Certificates of experience or employment, if any.
- Passport size photographs, if needed.
- Confirmation of application fee (where applicable).
Some universities may require certified translations in French or English. French student visa applications may require more documents such as proof of finances and accommodation where applicable.
Details available upon request.
